 What Luca Williams-Barnett needs to do to become Tottenham's next Harry Kane
 Tottenham academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett has been told not to let English football change him by ex-Spurs midfielder Micky Hazard
 View Image Luca Williams-Barnett is highly rated at Tottenham
 Add to preferred sources Comments Spurs George Sessions Press Association 15:17, 19 Nov 2026 Tottenham academy prospect Luca Williams-Barnett has been advised not to allow English football to alter his character ahead of a possible first start on Saturday.
 Williams-Barnett celebrated his 18th birthday just last month, yet has already made meaningful impacts in two substitute appearances during recent Premier League fixtures against Crystal Palace and Leeds.
 With Roberto De Zerbi facing a shortage of left-wing options due to injuries before Saturday's clash with Ipswich, the Italian manager may opt for Williams-Barnett, whom he has labelled a "special talent".
 Former Tottenham midfielder Micky Hazard featured alongside one of the north London side's finest academy graduates in Glenn Hoddle during a silverware-filled era in the 1980s.
 ‌ 
 Back in August, De Zerbi hosted 22 former players for lunch with his coaching staff and first-team squad at Hotspur Way, where Hazard immediately sought out Williams-Barnett, given the mounting anticipation surrounding the teenager in recent years.
 Make sure you never miss the latest Tottenham news and opinion by making football.london one of your Google preferred sources . 
 "I am a great believer in producing your own," Hazard, co-founder of mental health charity Legend on the Bench, told the Press Association. "What the homegrown do is they give the club its heart and soul because they know the importance of the club because they've come through the system.
 "When we talk about that we haven't produced a real superstar since Harry Kane, I have to be honest with you and say we have one in the making now. I think Luca's going to be something incredibly special.
 ‌ 
 "And the sooner we get him in that team, we can give him a chance to grow and develop because he's got the lot from what I've seen of him.
 "I spoke to him at the dinner, I sat next to him and I said to him, 'look Luca, please, all I ask of you, you're such a special talent and don't let English football change you', because I said, 'add to your game, add some of the things that they want you to add, but don't let them change you'.
 "I said, 'don't let them take away that flair, that genius and that creativity because that's you and that's who you are and that's who you are going to be. You're going to be in the Glenn Hoddle mould, the fans are going to idolise and worship you, but if you change and become this up and down, run around and tackle, and lose that natural instinct you have, it will only be you to blame'.
 "Glenn went through the same process where managers tried to add this and that or take away this and that, but he was strong enough mentally to stick to his game and look at the worship he has experienced.
 ‌ 
 "Luca could be the next... different to Glenn Hoddle, but that mould because he is very special."
 A Legend on the Bench park bench outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium was unveiled in September, with Hazard calling for additional installations alongside other Premier League and Football League clubs. Hazard, who established Legend on the Bench following the death of nephew Jay in 2019 and has installed more than 100 benches, said: "It is a further step along the line of getting as many benches as we can into the public domain to help saves lives.
 " Spurs doing what they have done hopefully means other Premier League and Football League clubs will be interested in having these benches."
 Talking Tottenham announces Christmas live show with Alasdair Gold and Ryan Taylor
 Talking Tottenham is heading out of the studio for a special festive live event at Signature Brew, Blackhorse Road on Thursday, 10 December 2026.
 football.london's dedicated Tottenham Hotspur correspondent Alasdair Gold will be joined on stage by Ryan Taylor and host Harry Brent for a full live show and podcast recording. They will be dissecting Spurs' season so far, analysing the team's form, diving into the upcoming January transfer window, and answering your burning questions about what lies ahead in N17.
 Because it's December, the night will also feature a dedicated festive Spurs pub quiz, giving fans the chance to test their Lilywhite knowledge and walk away with exclusive prizes, alongside an extended, unfiltered audience Q&A with the panel.
 The event takes place with doors opening at 6.30pm in the heart of Tottenham at Signature Brew’s working craft brewery, just a short walk from Blackhorse Road tube station.
 Capacity is strictly limited to keep the evening intimate. You can purchase your tickets here.
